message.content:
You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`; no internet), the repo layout, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: the chart family — `|chart|` (with series children `|bars|`, `|line|`, `|area|`, `|dots|`, `|bubble|`, `|band|`, `|mark|`, `|axis|`; cartesian, horizontal `direction: row`, and `direction: radial`; categories, numeric/time/log axes, fn: formulas with x / per-band u, samples, curve: linear/smooth/step, markers, labels, legend, tooltips (`tooltip: always|hover`), stacked/overlay bars, baseline, gridlines, ticks, step, range (incl. reversed), unit, format, clearance, per-datum fill/stroke lists, date literals) and `|pie|` (with `|slice|`, hole/donut). Make the output byte-identical to the original.

Where: `src/chart.rs` already has the hooks (`is_chart`, `measure`, `render`) wired into `layout::measure` and `render::render_node` for nodes whose computed `layout` is "chart" or "pie" (types `chart`/`pie` in types.rs set it). Put everything in chart.rs (+ helper modules if you like, e.g. src/chart/*.rs). The chart's title is its label: currently the Builder (scene.rs `build_node`) adds the label as a Text child for Block primitives — handle that as you see fit (keep shared-file edits small). Chart-related CSS rules (e.g. `.lini-chart-text { font-size: 12px; font-weight: normal; }`, `.lini-chart-tip { visibility: hidden; pointer-events: none; }`, `.lini-hit-0:hover ~ .lini-tip-0 { visibility: visible; }` were observed) go into `out.extra_rules` with a slot from `render::SLOT_ORDER` (add slots there if needed, in the order the original emits them); referenced palette vars must be registered with `crate::style::use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`. Also reproduce chart-specific diagnostics, e.g. `'|band|' belongs in a 'layout: chart'` (series types outside a chart), missing data errors, etc.

Test files (compare with `python3 /tmp/agent-tools/cmpw.py /tmp/bin-chart/executable <files>`): in /workspace/assets/test_doc_examples: prop_at, prop_axis, prop_bars, prop_baseline, prop_categories, prop_curve, prop_data, prop_fn, prop_format, prop_gridlines, prop_hole, prop_labels, prop_legend, prop_range, prop_side, prop_step, prop_ticks, prop_tooltip, prop_unit, prop_value, spec_33..spec_37, spec_56, spec_57, skill_05, blocks/skill_005, blocks/spec_034/037/056/057; and test_samples: charts.lini, chart_hero.lini, chart_advanced.lini. Then write many small synthetic charts in /tmp/<you>/ to pin down the formulas (axis tick selection "nice numbers", padding/gutters around plot, legend layout, label placement and collision rules, number formatting, colour walk order, smooth-curve control points, radial geometry, pie angles & label positions, tooltip markup). Charts nested in grids/rows must lay out correctly as ordinary nodes (their outer size).

Work iteratively: get the simplest bar chart byte-identical first, then expand feature by feature. Before committing, run the full asset comparison (`cmpw.py ... assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini assets/test_samples/*.lini`) and make sure nothing that passed before regresses (record the starting count: 71/209). Commit on your branch in your worktree and report: pass counts, what's implemented, shared-file edits, and known gaps.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. - Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/LICENSE). f87ace7 Link endpoint resolution with id scopes, auto-created endpoints, unworn class warnings f276df6 Merge highlight and fmt implementations; ignore .claude 025133c Merge branch 'worktree-agent-aab11fa07c95ee199' 793829f fmt: module overview 30b32c5 fmt: a drawing opens its block only with two or more subpaths 663cea6 fmt: math-language rules for binding right-hand sides 9cf6f84 fmt: != token, link right ends, escape error byte d12f965 fmt: tidy lexer/parser ffdfaed fmt: skip a leading byte-order mark 73066a8 fmt: diagnostic families/codes; parser uses fmt's syntax check for first errors; UTF-8 read errors a25b2f0 fmt: capsule paths, spaced class dots, link-op left ends, dim lexing context 9a131d0 fmt: verbatim call-arg prescan, label-block rules, dimension ops, path indices, more parse errors 99932f9 fmt: define-table resolution for row columns, sequential lifted rows e1c3e2c fmt: token-attached trivia model, transparent empty style blocks, rule/define edge cases bba3247 Implement lini highlight: structural/value/bar state machine with generated word lists 87969dd fmt: lexer-level math errors, hex colors, verbatim call args, more parse errors 61e22ca fmt: link chains, separators, exponents, draw subpaths e161525 fmt: canonical pretty-printer with its own lexer/parser 1d44ae3 Subcommand stubs, family hooks for charts, slot-ordered CSS 7edd38e CLI emulation, theme subcommand, gutters, canvas 20fba44 Add grid layout, shapes, geometric primitives, markers, bbox 8e13c94 Initial lini reimplementation skeleton: lexer, parser, styles, flow layout, SVG 12c27f9 Initial commit

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ticks.py v1 v2 ... : for each max value, run a single-bar chart and print the y tick labels
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
binp = '/workspace/executable'
tmpl = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 and '{}' in sys.argv[1] else None
vals = sys.argv[2:] if tmpl else sys.argv[1:]
if not tmpl:
    tmpl = '|chart| { categories: "a"; } [ |bars| { data: {}; } ]'
for v in vals:
    src = tmpl.replace('{}', v)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([binp, 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    labs = re.findall(r'class="lini-text lini-chart-text" x="([-0-9.]+)" y="([-0-9.]+)" dy="0.358em" style="fill: var\(--lini-muted\)">([^<]*)<', out)
    # y ticks: those with the same x-ish right edge on the left; just print texts
    print(v, '|', ' '.join(t for x, y, t in labs), '|', r.stderr.decode().strip())
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# labprobe.py: run snippets (template with {}) for values; print label position relative to the dot
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
tmpl = sys.argv[1]
vals = sys.argv[2:]
for v in vals:
    src = tmpl.replace('{}', v)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    dots = re.findall(r'lini-hit-(\d+) lini-oval"[^>]*transform="translate\(([-0-9.]+),([-0-9.]+)\)', out)
    labs = re.findall(r'chart-label" x="([-0-9.]+)" y="([-0-9.]+)"[^>]*>([^<]*)<', out)
    res = []
    for (k, dx, dy) in dots:
        k = int(k)
        if k < len(labs):
            lx, ly, t = labs[k]
            res.append('%s:(%+.2f,%+.2f)' % (t, float(lx) - float(dx), float(ly) - float(dy)))
    print(v, ' '.join(res), r.stderr.decode().strip()[:100])
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# splitprobe.py template values... : print the non-grid lines/polylines for each value
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
tmpl = sys.argv[1]
binp = os.environ.get('BIN', '/workspace/executable')
for v in sys.argv[2:]:
    src = tmpl.replace('{}', v)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([binp, 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    res = []
    lines = out.split('\n')
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.search(r'<polyline points="([^"]*)"', l)
        if m:
            pts = m.group(1).split()
            res.append('P%d[%s..%s]' % (len(pts), pts[0], pts[-1]))
            continue
        m = re.search(r'<line x1="([^"]*)" y1="([^"]*)" x2="([^"]*)" y2="([^"]*)"', l)
        if m and 'grid' not in lines[i - 1]:
            res.append('L(%s,%s->%s,%s)' % m.groups())
    print(v, ' '.join(res), r.stderr.decode().strip()[:100])
    os.remove(p)
    os.rmdir(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# dd.py name... : diff original vs ours for /tmp/chart/cases/<name>.lini (compact)
import subprocess, sys, os, difflib
ours = os.environ.get('BIN', '/tmp/bin-chart/executable')
n = int(os.environ.get('DL', '40'))
w = int(os.environ.get('W', '220'))
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    f = name if name.endswith('.lini') else '/tmp/chart/cases/%s.lini' % name
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f))
    b = os.path.basename(f)
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run([ours, b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    print('=====', name, 'exit', r1.returncode, r2.returncode)
    if r1.stderr != r2.stderr:
        print('stderr orig:', r1.stderr.decode()[:300])
        print('stderr ours:', r2.stderr.decode()[:300])
    a = r1.stdout.decode().split('\n')
    bb = r2.stdout.decode().split('\n')
    k = 0
    for l in difflib.unified_diff(a, bb, lineterm='', n=0):
        if l.startswith('---') or l.startswith('+++'):
            continue
        print(l[:w])
        k += 1
        if k >= n:
            break

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# fmtprobe.py fmt... : print tooltip texts (titles) for a bar chart with various values
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
vals = os.environ.get('VALS', '1234.5678, 0.0123, 0.5, 2.75, -3.125, 1, 0, 99999, 0.333333')
n = len(vals.split(','))
cats = ', '.join('"c%d"' % k for k in range(n))
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    src = '|chart| { categories: %s; format: %s; } [ |line| { data: %s; marker: dot; } ]' % (cats, f, vals)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    titles = re.findall(r'<title>c\d+: ([^<]*)</title>', out)
    ticks = re.findall(r'style="fill: var\(--lini-muted\)">([^<]*)<', out)
    print(f, '|', ' ; '.join(titles), '| ticks:', ' '.join(ticks[:8]), r.stderr.decode().strip()[:150])
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# xdom.py template vals... : print the x domain (from gridline/tick positions) and x tick labels
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
tmpl = sys.argv[1]
for v in sys.argv[2:]:
    src = tmpl.replace('{}', v)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    # plot extents from first horizontal gridline
    m = re.search(r'<line x1="([-0-9.]+)" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="([-0-9.]+)" y2="\2"/>', out)
    pl, pr = (float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(3))) if m else (None, None)
    # x tick labels: those at the max y among chart-text labels
    labs = re.findall(r'class="lini-text lini-chart-text" x="([-0-9.]+)" y="([-0-9.]+)" dy="0.358em" style="fill: var\(--lini-muted\)">([^<]*)<', out)
    if labs and pl is not None:
        ymax = max(float(y) for x, y, t in labs)
        xl = [(float(x), t) for x, y, t in labs if float(y) == ymax]
        # fit domain from two ticks
        res = ''
        try:
            vals = [(x, float(t)) for x, t in xl]
            if len(vals) >= 2:
                (x0, v0), (x1, v1) = vals[0], vals[-1]
                k = (x1 - x0) / (v1 - v0)
                lo = v0 - (x0 - pl) / k
                hi = v0 + (pr - x0) / k
                res = 'domain [%.4f, %.4f]' % (lo, hi)
        except Exception as e:
            res = str(e)
        print(v, '|', ' '.join(t for x, t in xl), '|', res, r.stderr.decode().strip()[:100])
    else:
        print(v, '| no labels', r.stderr.decode().strip()[:100])
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Collect run-length patterns of smooth lines from the original, and test candidate
# arithmetic for the samples against them.
import subprocess, os, re, tempfile, random, json, sys

def run_orig(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()

def collect(n_cases, seed):
    random.seed(seed)
    cases = []
    for _ in range(n_cases):
        npts = random.randint(3, 6)
        xs = sorted(random.sample(range(0, 20), npts))
        ys = [random.randint(1, 30) for _ in xs]
        data = ', '.join('%d %d' % (x, y) for x, y in zip(xs, ys))
        src = '|chart| [ |line| { data: %s; curve: smooth; } ]' % data
        out = run_orig(src)
        # plot rect
        m = re.search(r'<line x1="([-0-9.]+)" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="([-0-9.]+)" y2="\2"/>', out)
        hs = re.findall(r'<line x1="[-0-9.]+" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="[-0-9.]+" y2="\1"/>', out)
        pl, pr = float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(3))
        ys_px = [float(h) for h in hs]
        pb, pt = max(ys_px), min(ys_px)
        runs = []
        for mm in re.finditer(r'<(polyline points|line x1)="([^"]*)"', out):
            pass
        # series elements: lines after gridlines with rose-deep stroke
        series = re.findall(r'style="stroke: var\(--lini-rose-deep\)"[^>]*>\s*<(polyline points="([^"]*)"|line x1="([^"]*)" y1="([^"]*)" x2="([^"]*)" y2="([^"]*)")', out)
        for s in series:
            if s[1]:
                runs.append(len(s[1].split()))
            else:
                runs.append(2)
        # y domain from tick labels
        labs = re.findall(r'x="([-0-9.]+)" y="([-0-9.]+)" dy="0.358em" style="fill: var\(--lini-muted\)">([^<]*)<', out)
        cases.append({'xs': xs, 'ys': ys, 'pl': pl, 'pr': pr, 'pt': pt, 'pb': pb, 'runs': runs, 'out_has': len(series)})
    return cases

if __name__ == '__main__':
    cases = collect(int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]))
    json.dump(cases, open('/tmp/chart/smoothruns.json', 'w'))
    print(sum(1 for c in cases if len(c['runs']) > 1), 'split cases of', len(cases))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Categorical smooth lines: collect the original's sample points; fit the arithmetic.
import subprocess, os, re, tempfile, random, json, sys, math

def run_orig(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()

def f4(v):
    s = '%.4f' % v
    if '.' in s:
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
    return '0' if s == '-0' else s

def collect(n_cases, seed):
    random.seed(seed)
    cases = []
    for _ in range(n_cases):
        npts = random.randint(3, 7)
        ys = [random.randint(1, 60) for _ in range(npts)]
        cats = ', '.join('"c%d"' % k for k in range(npts))
        src = '|chart| { categories: %s; } [ |line| { data: %s; curve: smooth; } ]' % (cats, ', '.join(map(str, ys)))
        out = run_orig(src)
        m = re.search(r'<line x1="([-0-9.]+)" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="([-0-9.]+)" y2="\2"/>', out)
        hs = re.findall(r'<line x1="[-0-9.]+" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="[-0-9.]+" y2="\1"/>', out)
        pl, pr = float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(3))
        yv = [float(h) for h in hs]
        pb, pt = max(yv), min(yv)
        pts = []
        series = re.findall(r'style="stroke: var\(--lini-rose-deep\)"[^>]*>\s*<(?:polyline points="([^"]*)"|line x1="([^"]*)" y1="([^"]*)" x2="([^"]*)" y2="([^"]*)")', out)
        runs = []
        for s in series:
            if s[0]:
                pp = s[0].split()
            else:
                pp = ['%s,%s' % (s[1], s[2]), '%s,%s' % (s[3], s[4])]
            runs.append(len(pp))
            pts += pp if not pts else pp[1:]
        cases.append({'ys': ys, 'pl': pl, 'pr': pr, 'pt': pt, 'pb': pb, 'runs': runs, 'pts': pts})
    return cases

if __name__ == '__main__':
    cases = collect(int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]))
    json.dump(cases, open('/tmp/chart/smoothcat.json', 'w'))
    print(sum(1 for c in cases if len(c['runs']) > 1), 'split cases of', len(cases))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Use polyline run splits as an oracle for the exact arithmetic of the plot rectangle.
import subprocess, os, re, tempfile, random, json, sys, math
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/chart')
exec(open('/tmp/chart/clipsim.py').read().split('def yform')[0])  # clip_runs

def run_orig(src):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)
    return r.stdout.decode()

def nice_step(span):
    p = 10 ** (math.floor(math.log10(span / 5)) - 1)
    for _ in range(40):
        for m in (1, 2, 5):
            s = m * p
            if span / s <= 5 + 1e-9:
                return s
        p *= 10
    return p

def snap(q):
    return round(q) if abs(q - round(q)) < 1e-9 else q

def collect(n_cases, seed, title, legend, xtitle, width=360, height=220):
    random.seed(seed)
    cases = []
    for _ in range(n_cases):
        npts = random.randint(4, 8)
        ys = [random.randint(1, 60) for _ in range(npts)]
        cats = ', '.join('"c%d"' % k for k in range(npts))
        t = '"Title" ' if title else ''
        extra = '|line| "B" { data: %s; }' % ', '.join('1' for _ in ys) if legend else ''
        name = '"A" ' if legend else ''
        xt = '|axis| "XT" { side: bottom; }' if xtitle else ''
        src = '|chart| %s{ categories: %s; width: %d; height: %d; } [ %s; |line| %s{ data: %s; }; %s ]' % (t, cats, width, height, xt, name, ', '.join(map(str, ys)), extra)
        out = run_orig(src)
        m = re.search(r'<line x1="([-0-9.]+)" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="([-0-9.]+)" y2="\2"/>', out)
        hs = re.findall(r'<line x1="[-0-9.]+" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="[-0-9.]+" y2="\1"/>', out)
        pl, pr = float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(3))
        yv = [float(h) for h in hs]
        pb, pt = max(yv), min(yv)
        series = re.findall(r'style="stroke: var\(--lini-rose-deep\)"[^>]*>\s*<(?:polyline points="([^"]*)"|line x1="([^"]*)")', out)
        runs = [len(s[0].split()) if s[0] else 2 for s in series]
        cases.append({'ys': ys, 'pl': pl, 'pr': pr, 'pt': pt, 'pb': pb, 'runs': runs})
    return cases

def check(cases, plf, prf, ptf, pbf):
    bad = 0
    for c in cases:
        ys = c['ys']; n = len(ys)
        pl, pr, pt, pb = plf(c), prf(c), ptf(c), pbf(c)
        mx = max(ys); st = nice_step(mx); yhi = math.ceil(snap(mx / st)) * st
        X = [pl + (pr - pl) * ((k + 0.5) / n) for k in range(n)]
        Y = [pb - ((y - 0) / (yhi - 0)) * (pb - pt) for y in ys]
        eps = 1e-9
        runs = [len(r) for r in clip_runs(list(zip(X, Y)), [pl - eps, pt - eps, pr + eps, pb + eps])]
        if runs != c['runs']:
            bad += 1
    return bad

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, sys, math, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/chart')
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/scripts')
from layoutfit import check, nice_step, snap
from tw import tw

W, H = 380.0, 270.0
cl, cr, ct, cb = -W / 2, W / 2, -H / 2, H / 2
c = 6.0
g = 15.0

def fmt_tick(v, s):
    # decimals of step
    for d in range(12):
        x = s * 10 ** d
        if abs(x - round(x)) < 1e-6 * max(abs(x), 1):
            break
    t = '%.*f' % (d, v)
    if '.' in t:
        t = t.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
    return t

def wmax(case):
    mx = max(case['ys']); st = nice_step(mx); hi = math.ceil(snap(mx / st)) * st
    ticks = [k * st for k in range(int(round(hi / st)) + 1)]
    return max(tw(fmt_tick(v, st), 12, 400) for v in ticks)

PL = {
    'a': lambda cs: ((cl + 4.0) + wmax(cs)) + c,
    'b': lambda cs: cl + (4.0 + wmax(cs) + c),
    'c': lambda cs: cl + 4.0 + (wmax(cs) + c),
    'd': lambda cs: (cl + (wmax(cs) + c)) + 4.0,
}
PR = {'a': lambda cs: cr - 12.0}

def mk(layout):
    title, legend, xt = layout
    pts = {}
    # top
    if title:
        pts['t1'] = lambda cs: ct + 8.0 + 18.0 + g
        pts['t2'] = lambda cs: ct + (8.0 + 18.0 + g)
        pts['t3'] = lambda cs: (ct + 8.0) + (18.0 + g)
        pts['t4'] = lambda cs: ct + 41.0
        pts['t5'] = lambda cs: ct + 8.0 + 10.5 + 7.5 + g
    else:
        pts['t1'] = lambda cs: ct + 8.0
    pbs = {}
    stack = c + 14.8 + (22.8 if xt else 0.0)
    if legend:
        pbs['b1'] = lambda cs: cb - 16.4 - g - (c + 14.8) - (22.8 if xt else 0)
        pbs['b2'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - (c + 14.8) - 23.4 - (22.8 if xt else 0)
        pbs['b3'] = lambda cs: cb - 10.8 - 6.0 - g + 0.4 - (c + 14.8) - (22.8 if xt else 0)
        pbs['b4'] = lambda cs: (cb - 16.4 - g) - stack
        pbs['b5'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - stack - 23.4
        pbs['b6'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - (8.4 + g) - stack
        pbs['b7'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - stack - (8.4 + g)
        pbs['b8'] = lambda cs: cb - (16.4 + g) - stack
        pbs['b9'] = lambda cs: cb - 10.8 - 6.0 - g + 0.4 - stack
        pbs['b10'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - (22.8 if xt else 0) - (c + 14.8) - 23.4
        pbs['b11'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - 23.4 - (22.8 if xt else 0) - (c + 14.8)
    else:
        pbs['b1'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - stack
        pbs['b2'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - (22.8 if xt else 0) - (c + 14.8)
        pbs['b3'] = lambda cs: cb - (8.0 + stack)
        pbs['b4'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - (c + 14.8) - (22.8 if xt else 0)
        pbs['b5'] = lambda cs: cb - 8.0 - c - 14.8 - (22.8 if xt else 0)
    return pts, pbs

layouts = {'plain': (0, 0, 0), 'title': (1, 0, 0), 'legend': (0, 1, 0), 'tl': (1, 1, 0), 'xt': (0, 0, 1), 'all': (1, 1, 1)}
for name, lay in layouts.items():
    cases = json.load(open('/tmp/chart/lay_%s.json' % name))
    pts, pbs = mk(lay)
    res = []
    for (kl, plf), (kt, ptf), (kb, pbf) in itertools.product(PL.items(), pts.items(), pbs.items()):
        bad = check(cases, plf, PR['a'], ptf, pbf)
        res.append((bad, kl, kt, kb))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Collect split data for layouts with gap / y titles / band labels and fit pt, pb expressions.
import json, sys, math, itertools, random, re, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/chart')
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/scripts')
from layoutfit import check, nice_step, snap, run_orig
from tw import tw

def collect(n, seed, title, legend, xt, yt, band, gap, W=380, H=270):
    random.seed(seed)
    cases = []
    for _ in range(n):
        npts = random.randint(4, 8)
        ys = [random.randint(1, 60) for _ in range(npts)]
        cats = ', '.join('"c%d"' % k for k in range(npts))
        t = '"Title" ' if title else ''
        parts = []
        if xt:
            parts.append('|axis| "XT" { side: bottom; }')
        if yt:
            parts.append('|axis| "YT" { side: left; }')
        if band:
            parts.append('|band| "BB" { range: 0 1; fill: --sky; }')
        parts.append('|line| %s{ data: %s; }' % ('"A" ' if legend else '', ', '.join(map(str, ys))))
        if legend:
            parts.append('|line| "B" { data: %s; }' % ', '.join('1' for _ in ys))
        g = 'gap: %g; ' % gap if gap is not None else ''
        src = '|chart| %s{ %scategories: %s; width: %d; height: %d; } [ %s ]' % (t, g, cats, W, H, '; '.join(parts))
        out = run_orig(src)
        m = re.search(r'<line x1="([-0-9.]+)" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="([-0-9.]+)" y2="\2"/>', out)
        if not m:
            print(src)
            print(out[:500])
            raise SystemExit
        hs = re.findall(r'<line x1="[-0-9.]+" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="[-0-9.]+" y2="\1"/>', out)
        pl, pr = float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(3))
        yv = [float(h) for h in hs]
        series = re.findall(r'style="stroke: var\(--lini-rose-deep\)"[^>]*>\s*<(?:polyline points="([^"]*)"|line x1="([^"]*)")', out)
        runs = [len(s[0].split()) if s[0] else 2 for s in series]
        cases.append({'ys': ys, 'pl': pl, 'pr': pr, 'pt': min(yv), 'pb': max(yv), 'runs': runs})
    return cases

if __name__ == '__main__':
    configs = {
        'g10_tl': (1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 10),
        'g10_all': (1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 10),
        'yt': (0, 0, 0, 1, 0, None),
        'yt_title': (1, 0, 0, 1, 0, None),
        'band': (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, None),
        'band_xt': (0, 0, 1, 0, 1, None),
        'band_leg_xt': (0, 1, 1, 0, 1, None),
        'g7_yt_title_leg': (1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 7),
    }
    for name, cfg in configs.items():
        cs = collect(120, 23, *cfg)
        json.dump(cs, open('/tmp/chart/lay3_%s.json' % name, 'w'))
        print(name, sum(1 for c in cs if len(c['runs']) > 1))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ydom.py template vals... : print the y domain implied by the y tick labels & plot rect
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
tmpl = sys.argv[1]
for v in sys.argv[2:]:
    src = tmpl.replace('{}', v)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)
    hs = re.findall(r'<line x1="([-0-9.]+)" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="([-0-9.]+)" y2="\2"/>', out)
    labs = re.findall(r'class="lini-text lini-chart-text" x="([-0-9.]+)" y="([-0-9.]+)" dy="0.358em" style="fill: var\(--lini-muted\)">([^<]*)<', out)
    if not hs or not labs:
        print(v, '| ?', r.stderr.decode().strip()[:100]); continue
    pl = float(hs[0][0])
    ys = [float(h[1]) for h in hs]
    # y labels: left of the plot
    yl = [(float(y), t) for x, y, t in labs if float(x) < pl]
    try:
        vals = [(y, float(t)) for y, t in yl]
    except ValueError:
        print(v, '| nonnumeric'); continue
    # plot top/bottom: find from the extent of the first polyline/line? use chart default: estimate via labels

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ydom.py template vals... : print the y domain implied by the y tick labels & plot rect
import subprocess, sys, os, re, tempfile
tmpl = sys.argv[1]
for v in sys.argv[2:]:
    src = tmpl.replace('{}', v)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp/chart')
    p = os.path.join(d, 'r_in.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'r_in.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    out = r.stdout.decode()
    os.remove(p); os.rmdir(d)
    hs = re.findall(r'<line x1="([-0-9.]+)" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="([-0-9.]+)" y2="\2"/>', out)
    labs = re.findall(r'class="lini-text lini-chart-text" x="([-0-9.]+)" y="([-0-9.]+)" dy="0.358em" style="fill: var\(--lini-muted\)">([^<]*)<', out)
    if not hs or not labs:
        print(v, '| ?', r.stderr.decode().strip()[:100]); continue
    pl = float(hs[0][0])
    ys = [float(h[1]) for h in hs]
    # y labels: left of the plot
    yl = [(float(y), t) for x, y, t in labs if float(x) < pl]
    try:
        vals = [(y, float(t)) for y, t in yl]
    except ValueError:
        print(v, '| nonnumeric'); continue
    # plot top/bottom: find from the extent of the first polyline/line? use chart default: estimate via labels
    (y0, v0), (y1, v1) = vals[0], vals[-1]
    k = (y1 - y0) / (v1 - v0)
    # plot top/bottom are min/max of horizontal gridline extents only if ticks hit them; use known rect from polyline env
    m = re.search(r'<line x1="([-0-9.]+)" y1="([-0-9.]+)" x2="\1" y2="([-0-9.]+)"/>', out)
    print(v, '| ticks', ' '.join(t for y, t in yl), '| px/unit %.4f' % k, '| y(lo end)=', '%.4f' % (v0 + (81.2 - y0) / k), 'y(hi end)=', '%.4f' % (v0 + (-102 - y0) / k))

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# dd.py name... : diff original vs ours for /tmp/chart/cases/<name>.lini (compact)
import subprocess, sys, os, difflib
ours = os.environ.get('BIN', '/tmp/bin-chart/executable')
n = int(os.environ.get('DL', '40'))
w = int(os.environ.get('W', '220'))
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    f = name if name.endswith('.lini') else '/tmp/chart/cases/%s.lini' % name
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f))
    b = os.path.basename(f)
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run([ours, b], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    print('=====', name, 'exit', r1.returncode, r2.returncode)
    if r1.stderr != r2.stderr:
        print('stderr orig:', r1.stderr.decode()[:300])
        print('stderr ours:', r2.stderr.decode()[:300])
    a = r1.stdout.decode().split('\n')
    bb = r2.stdout.decode().split('\n')
    k = 0
    for l in difflib.unified_diff(a, bb, lineterm='', n=0):
        if l.startswith('---') or l.startswith('+++'):
            continue
        print(l[:w])
        k += 1
        if k >= n:
            break

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# mutate.py: generate variants of the chart asset files into /tmp/chart/mut/
import os, re, sys
src_files = open('/tmp/chart/charttests.txt').read().split()
out = '/tmp/chart/mut'
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
for f in os.listdir(out):
    os.remove(os.path.join(out, f))
root = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a4df1b014475aff8e/'

def hdr_insert(text, decl):
    # insert decl into every |chart| / |pie| header block that has one: |chart| "T" { ...
    return re.sub(r'(\|(?:chart|pie)\|[^{\[\n]*\{)', lambda m: m.group(1) + ' ' + decl, text)

muts = {
    'tipalways': lambda t: hdr_insert(t, 'tooltip: always;'),
    'tipnone': lambda t: hdr_insert(t, 'tooltip: none;'),
    'small': lambda t: hdr_insert(re.sub(r'width: \d+; height: \d+;', '', t), 'width: 300; height: 200;'),
    'big': lambda t: hdr_insert(re.sub(r'width: \d+; height: \d+;', '', t), 'width: 520; height: 340;'),
    'clear0': lambda t: hdr_insert(t, 'clearance: 2;'),
    'gap5': lambda t: hdr_insert(t, 'gap: 5;'),
    'row': lambda t: hdr_insert(re.sub(r'direction: \w+;', '', t), 'direction: row;'),
    'col': lambda t: re.sub(r'direction: row;', '', t),
    'stacked': lambda t: hdr_insert(re.sub(r'bars: \w+;', '', t), 'bars: stacked;'),
    'overlay': lambda t: hdr_insert(re.sub(r'bars: \w+;', '', t), 'bars: overlay;'),
    'smooth': lambda t: re.sub(r'(\|(?:line|area)\|[^{\n]*\{)', lambda m: m.group(1) + ' curve: smooth;', re.sub(r'curve: \w+;', '', t)),
    'step': lambda t: re.sub(r'(\|(?:line|area)\|[^{\n]*\{)', lambda m: m.group(1) + ' curve: step;', re.sub(r'curve: \w+;', '', t)),
    'markers': lambda t: re.sub(r'(\|(?:line|area)\|[^{\n]*\{)', lambda m: m.group(1) + ' marker: dot;', re.sub(r'marker: \w+;', '', t)),
    'notitle': lambda t: re.sub(r'(\|(?:chart|pie)\|) "[^"]*"', r'\1', t),
    'fmt1': lambda t: hdr_insert(t, 'format: decimal 1;'),
}
n = 0
for f in src_files:
    t = open(root + f if not f.startswith('/') else f).read()
    if '|chart|' not in t and '|pie|' not in t:
        continue
    base = os.path.basename(f)[:-5]
    for name, fn in muts.items():
        t2 = fn(t)
        if t2 == t:
            continue
        open(os.path.join(out, '%s__%s.lini' % (base, name)), 'w').write(t2)
        n += 1
print(n, 'variants')

import subprocess, re, sys, os
# hermfit.py file.lini shape_index knot_start knot_count
f, shape, k0, kn = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
orig = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
shapes = re.findall(r'<(?:polyline|polygon|line) ([^/]*)/>', orig)
pts = [p.split(',') for p in re.search(r'points="([^"]*)"', shapes[shape]).group(1).split(' ')]
dbg = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-chart/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, env=dict(os.environ, LINI_DBG_SMOOTH='1')).stderr.decode()
knots = [tuple(float(v) for v in l.split()[1:]) for l in dbg.splitlines() if l.startswith('KNOT')]
knots = knots[k0:k0 + kn]
def f4(v):
    s = '%.4f' % v
    if '.' in s:
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
    if s == '-0':
        s = '0'
    return s
from fractions import Fraction
def variants(x0, y0, m0, x1, y1, m1, t):
    h = x1 - x0
    t2 = t * t
    t3 = t2 * t
    out = {}
    out['mine'] = (2*t3 - 3*t2 + 1)*y0 + (t3 - 2*t2 + t)*h*m0 + (-2*t3 + 3*t2)*y1 + (t3 - t2)*h*m1
    # bezier with control points
    c1 = y0 + m0 * h / 3
    c2 = y1 - m1 * h / 3
    u = 1 - t
    out['bez'] = u*u*u*y0 + 3*u*u*t*c1 + 3*u*t*t*c2 + t*t*t*y1
    out['bez2'] = u**3*y0 + 3*u**2*t*c1 + 3*u*t**2*c2 + t**3*y1
    # de casteljau
    a = y0 + (c1 - y0)*t; bb = c1 + (c2 - c1)*t; cc = c2 + (y1 - c2)*t
    d1 = a + (bb - a)*t; d2 = bb + (cc - bb)*t
    out['decas'] = d1 + (d2 - d1)*t
    a = y0*u + c1*t; bb = c1*u + c2*t; cc = c2*u + y1*t
    d1 = a*u + bb*t; d2 = bb*u + cc*t
    out['decas2'] = d1*u + d2*t
    # hermite with h*m precomputed
    hm0 = h*m0; hm1 = h*m1
    out['herm_hm'] = (2*t3 - 3*t2 + 1)*y0 + (t3 - 2*t2 + t)*hm0 + (-2*t3 + 3*t2)*y1 + (t3 - t2)*hm1
    # polynomial form: y0 + t*(hm0) + t2*(3(y1-y0) - 2hm0 - hm1) + t3*(2(y0-y1) + hm0 + hm1)
    dy = y1 - y0
    out['poly'] = y0 + hm0*t + (3*dy - 2*hm0 - hm1)*t2 + (-2*dy + hm0 + hm1)*t3
    out['polyH'] = y0 + t*(hm0 + t*((3*dy - 2*hm0 - hm1) + t*(-2*dy + hm0 + hm1)))
    # x-space evaluation: s = x - x0
    s = h * t
    c2_ = (3*dy/h - 2*m0 - m1)/h

import subprocess, re, sys, os
# Fit the value->pixel mapping using smooth-curve tie points.
# For each case: run ours with LINI_DBG_SMOOTH to get knots (x exact, y exact in our mapping),
# and LINI_DBG_GEO for pt/pb/lo/hi; then recompute knots via variants.
def f4(v):
    s = '%.4f' % v
    if '.' in s:
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
    if s == '-0':
        s = '0'
    return s

def fc(pts):
    n = len(pts)
    d = []
    hs = []
    for k in range(n - 1):
        h = pts[k + 1][0] - pts[k][0]
        hs.append(h)
        d.append(0.0 if h == 0 else (pts[k + 1][1] - pts[k][1]) / h)
    m = [0.0] * n
    m[0] = d[0]
    m[n - 1] = d[n - 2]
    for k in range(1, n - 1):
        m[k] = 0.0 if d[k - 1] * d[k] <= 0 else (d[k - 1] + d[k]) / 2
    for k in range(n - 1):
        if d[k] == 0:
            m[k] = 0.0
            m[k + 1] = 0.0
            continue
        a = m[k] / d[k]
        b = m[k + 1] / d[k]
        s = a * a + b * b
        if s > 9:
            t = 3 / s ** 0.5
            m[k] = t * a * d[k]
            m[k + 1] = t * b * d[k]
    return m, hs

def herm(pts, m, hs):
    out = [pts[0]]
    for k in range(len(pts) - 1):
        x0, y0 = pts[k]
        y1 = pts[k + 1][1]
        h = hs[k]
        for j in range(1, 17):
            t = j / 16
            t2 = t * t
            t3 = t2 * t
            x = x0 + h * t
            y = (2 * t3 - 3 * t2 + 1) * y0 + (t3 - 2 * t2 + t) * h * m[k] + (-2 * t3 + 3 * t2) * y1 + (t3 - t2) * h * m[k + 1]
            out.append((x, y))
    return out

maps = {
    'mine': lambda v, lo, hi, pt, pb: pb - ((v - lo) / (hi - lo)) * (pb - pt),
    'fromtop': lambda v, lo, hi, pt, pb: pt + (hi - v) / (hi - lo) * (pb - pt),
    'fromtop2': lambda v, lo, hi, pt, pb: pt + (pb - pt) * ((hi - v) / (hi - lo)),
    'scale': lambda v, lo, hi, pt, pb: pb + (v - lo) * ((pt - pb) / (hi - lo)),
    'mul_first': lambda v, lo, hi, pt, pb: pb - (v - lo) * (pb - pt) / (hi - lo),
    'lerp2': lambda v, lo, hi, pt, pb: pb * (1 - (v - lo) / (hi - lo)) + pt * ((v - lo) / (hi - lo)),
    'lerp3': lambda v, lo, hi, pt, pb: (pb * (hi - v) + pt * (v - lo)) / (hi - lo),
    'plus': lambda v, lo, hi, pt, pb: pb + ((v - lo) / (hi - lo)) * (pt - pb),
}

cases = sys.argv[1:]
tot = {k: 0 for k in maps}
for spec in cases:
    f, shape = spec.split(':')
    shape = int(shape)
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    orig = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
    shapes = re.findall(r'<(?:polyline|polygon|line) ([^/]*)/>', orig)
    opts = [p.split(',') for p in re.search(r'points="([^"]*)"', shapes[shape]).group(1).split(' ')]
    dbg = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-chart/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, env=dict(os.environ, LINI_DBG_SMOOTH='1')).stderr.decode()
    geo = [l.split()[1:] for l in dbg.splitlines() if l.startswith('GEO')]
    vals = [l.split()[1:] for l in dbg.splitlines() if l.startswith('VALS')]
    knots = [tuple(float(v) for v in l.split()[1:]) for l in dbg.splitlines() if l.startswith('KNOT')]
    # find which series matches this shape: first knot x/y vs orig first point
    pt_, pb_, lo, hi = [float(x) for x in geo[0]]
    # group knots by series: VALS lines give the values per smooth series in order
    series = [[float(x) for x in v] for v in vals]
    pos = 0
    chosen = None
    for sv in series:
        ks = knots[pos:pos + len(sv)]
        pos += len(sv)
        if f4(ks[0][0]) == opts[0][0] and f4(ks[0][1]) == opts[0][1]:
            chosen = (sv, ks)
    if not chosen:
        print('no series match', spec); continue
    sv, ks = chosen
    for name, mp in maps.items():
        pts = [(ks[k][0], mp(sv[k], lo, hi, pt_, pb_)) for k in range(len(sv))]
        m, hs = fc(pts)
        out = herm(pts, m, hs)
        bad = sum(1 for (x, y), o in zip(out, opts) if f4(y) != o[1] or f4(x) != o[0])
        tot[name] += bad
    print(spec, {k: v for k, v in tot.items()})
print('TOTAL', tot)

import subprocess, re, sys, os, math
def f4(v):
    s = '%.4f' % v
    if '.' in s:
        s = s.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
    if s == '-0':
        s = '0'
    return s
def ulps(x, k):
    for _ in range(abs(k)):
        x = math.nextafter(x, math.inf if k > 0 else -math.inf)
    return x
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b = os.path.basename(f)
    orig = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d).stdout.decode()
    dbg = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-chart/executable', b], capture_output=True, cwd=d, env=dict(os.environ, LINI_DBG_SMOOTH='1')).stderr.decode()
    geo = [l.split()[1:] for l in dbg.splitlines() if l.startswith('GEO')]
    pt, pb, lo, hi, pl, pr = [float(x) for x in geo[0][:6]]
    n = int(geo[0][6])
    polys = re.findall(r'<polyline points="([^"]*)"', orig)
    cand = [p for p in polys if len(p.split(' ')) == 16 * (n - 1) + 1]
    opts = [p.split(',') for p in cand[0].split(' ')]
    res = []
    for dk in range(-6, 7):
        pl2 = ulps(pl, dk)
        xs = [pl2 + (pr - pl2) * ((k + 0.5) / n) for k in range(n)]
        bad = 0
        for k in range(n - 1):
            for j in range(0, 17):
                t = j / 16
                x = xs[k] + (xs[k + 1] - xs[k]) * t
                if f4(x) != opts[k * 16 + j][0]:
                    bad += 1
        res.append((dk, bad))
    print(f, repr(pl), res)

def f4(v):
    s = '%.4f' % v

    if s == '-0':
        s = '0'
    return s
def fc(pts):
    n = len(pts)
    d = []
    hs = []
    for k in range(n - 1):
        h = pts[k + 1][0] - pts[k][0]
        hs.append(h)
        d.append(0.0 if h == 0 else (pts[k + 1][1] - pts[k][1]) / h)
    m = [0.0] * n
    m[0] = d[0]
    m[n - 1] = d[n - 2]
    for k in range(1, n - 1):
        m[k] = 0.0 if d[k - 1] * d[k] <= 0 else (d[k - 1] + d[k]) / 2
    for k in range(n - 1):
        if d[k] == 0:
            m[k] = 0.0
            m[k + 1] = 0.0
            continue
        a = m[k] / d[k]
        b = m[k + 1] / d[k]
        s = a * a + b * b
        if s > 9:
            t = 3 / s ** 0.5
            m[k] = t * a * d[k]
            m[k + 1] = t * b * d[k]
    return m, hs
def herm(pts, m, hs):
    out = [pts[0]]
    for k in range(len(pts) - 1):
        x0, y0 = pts[k]
        y1 = pts[k + 1][1]
        h = hs[k]
        for j in range(1, 17):
            t = j / 16
            t2 = t * t
            t3 = t2 * t
            x = x0 + h * t
            y = (2 * t3 - 3 * t2 + 1) * y0 + (t3 - 2 * t2 + t) * h * m[k] + (-2 * t3 + 3 * t2) * y1 + (t3 - t2) * h * m[k + 1]
            out.append((x, y))
    return out

    'P1': lambda cb, c: (cb - 8) - (c + 14.8),
    'P2': lambda cb, c: ((cb - 8) - c) - 14.8,
    'P3': lambda cb, c: ((cb - 8) - 14.8) - c,
    'P4': lambda cb, c: cb - (8 + (c + 14.8)),
    'P5': lambda cb, c: cb - ((8 + c) + 14.8),
    'P7': lambda cb, c: (cb - (c + 14.8)) - 8,
    'P8': lambda cb, c: cb - (c + (14.8 + 8)),
    'P9': lambda cb, c: (cb - 22.8) - c,
    'P10': lambda cb, c: (cb - 8) - (14.8 + c),
}
